name: std::pmr::unsynchronized_pool_resource::do_allocate
intro:
Allocates storage.

If the pool selected for a block of size bytes is unable to satisfy the request from its internal data structures, calls allocate() on the upstream memory resource to obtain memory.

If the size requested is larger than what the largest pool can handle, memory is allocated by calling allocate() on the upstream memory resource.

sections.title: Return value
sections.text: A pointer to allocated storage of at least bytes bytes in size, aligned to the specified alignment if such alignment is supported, and to alignof(std::max_align_t) otherwise.

sections.title: Exceptions
sections.text: Throws nothing unless calling allocate() on the upstream memory resource throws.

examples.title: Practical use case
examples.input: Allocate, construct, destroy, and release storage. Public allocate/deallocate/is_equal dispatch to each resource's protected do_* implementation.
